EXT.evidence: Gives a running commentary of what is happening and directs the other person (“wait,” “run”), saying they’ve been “spelling out the situation” and narrating what they see (u019–u021).

AGR.evidence: Provides information and a warning, but shows neither clear warmth/generosity nor hostility; no strong cues either way.

CON.evidence: Misreports a key quote (“I have a bomb” vs. “I am your mom,” u015–u017) and admits not knowing what’s going on (u019), suggesting carelessness with details.

NEU.evidence: Expresses uncertainty and alarm—doesn’t know what’s happening, can’t hear anything, then urgently says to run as others approach (u019–u021).

OPN.evidence: Accepts a correction that makes more sense (u017), but overall shows no strong curiosity or imaginative exploration; the misquote indicates confusion rather than openness.
